A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEAM and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, efficiency, ablation, transfer, and scaling experiments in Sections 4–5, plus model outputs in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a GRPO (LoRA) efficiency result in Table 3.

M1.justification: The experience schema, frozen executor, binary reward, GRPO training, and optional deployment-time SFT remain unchanged. Alternative schemas and feedback signals are discussed as possibilities, without an implemented procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use DAPO training data, the same four mathematics benchmarks, and CodeContests, MBPP, HotpotQA, and Natural Questions for cross-domain evaluation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds GRPO (LoRA) to the efficiency comparison and labels the existing GRPO row GRPO (Full). Comparator membership in the main accuracy comparison, Table 1, is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample counts, decoding procedures, metrics, and hardware remain unchanged. The new LoRA comparator uses the existing AIME25 efficiency setup; no separate evaluation protocol or revision to existing experimental settings is specified.

E4.justification: The training-regime ablation, model-pairing and transfer analyses, cross-domain tests, experience scaling, and Appendix C case study are retained. Table 3 adds comparator scores without a distinct new ablation, robustness test, or analytical procedure.

E5.justification: Both retain means over 10 independent runs, 10 random evaluation splits for the ablation, randomized ordering for online baselines, and one execution per instance for efficiency measurement. No uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: The new GRPO (LoRA) row in Table 3 reports 104 GPU-hours, 0.81 seconds per instance, and 2.51 seconds time-to-correct, matching the retained GRPO (Full) values. Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11) retain their mathematical content. Equation (7) abbreviates the same reward condition, and the expanded TTC caption explains the existing definition. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: utility-trained parametric experience generation for frozen executors, low overhead, and optional improvement through logged-success SFT.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly qualifies the schema as especially suitable for procedural domains, while Section 3.3 discusses preferences and judge assessments as possible utility signals. The limitations more explicitly frame executor specificity as a design tradeoff and distinguish demonstrated results from broader transfer and continual adaptation.

D1.justification: The code-access reference changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to Cocobalt/SEAM on GitHub. Table 3 explicitly identifies full-parameter and LoRA training. Appendix implementation details remain unchanged, with no LoRA-specific hyperparameters supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work section and cited works remain unchanged. SEAM retains its positioning against retrieval-based experience reuse and direct executor training.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanations in Sections 3.1–3.3, rewrites the limitations, updates affiliations and author notes, and adds acknowledgments. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains a row and an expanded caption. Existing tables and figures reflow across columns and pages, including the appendix prompts and hyperparameter tables. The method diagram and result graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves conceptual clarity by explaining the schema's applicability and distinguishing the tested reward from possible alternatives. The added LoRA comparison broadens the efficiency evidence, although missing LoRA-specific settings limit reproducibility. These are limited gains; the central method and accuracy evidence remain unchanged.
